Different "trace conditions" extract varying amounts of diagnostic information from this raw trace — from nothing (no_trace: code only) to everything (full_trace: complete line-by-line log). Each representation is paired with source code and fed to an SFT language model to predict the test verdict (pass/fail). The key finding: compact exception summaries achieve 99%+ accuracy, while verbose complete traces degrade performance to 72-82%.

LAYOUT: Horizontal left-to-right flow. Four logical stages. The center "Trace Conditions" stage is the visual focal point (~45% of width), fanning out vertically into 4 parallel paths.

=== STAGE 1: INPUT (left, ~12% width) ===
A single elegant rounded box containing two visually distinct sub-sections stacked vertically:
- Top sub-section: a miniature code block icon — 4-5 thin horizontal lines in monospace gray (#78909C) representing Python source code, with a small "def solve(...):" label in 8pt monospace at top
- Divider: a thin dashed line (#E0E0E0)
- Bottom sub-section: a miniature terminal prompt icon — ">>> test()" in 8pt monospace dark gray
Box background: #FAFBFC. Border: #CFD8DC, 1px. Corner radius 10px.
Subtle drop shadow: 2px offset down-right, rgba(0,0,0,0.06).
Label below box: "Source Code + Test" in 9pt serif, #546E7A.

=== STAGE 2: EXECUTION ENGINE (left of center, ~8% width) ===
A compact rounded box or badge:
- Icon: a small gear ⚙ or play-triangle ▶ symbol in #546E7A
- Label: "Execute" in 9pt serif bold
- Background: #ECEFF1, border: #B0BEC5 1px, corner radius 10px
Thin elegant arrow from Stage 1 → Stage 2: stroke #90A4AE, 1.2pt, small filled arrowhead.

=== STAGE 3: TRACE CONDITIONS (center, ~45% width — VISUAL FOCUS) ===

On the left edge of this stage, show a "Raw Trace" document icon:
- A tall narrow rectangle (like a scrolled document/log) with ~15 tiny horizontal lines representing trace output
- The lines should have varying lengths to look like real log output
- Background: white, border: #B0BEC5
- A wavy/torn bottom edge suggesting the trace continues (hundreds more lines)
- Small label: "Raw Trace" in 8pt serif italic, #78909C
- Tiny line count annotation: "~2048 lines" in 7pt gray

From this raw trace document, four horizontal extraction arrows branch out to the RIGHT, vertically stacked (evenly spaced), each leading to a representation card:

**Path 1 — no_trace (top):**
Arrow: thin dotted line (#BDBDBD, 0.8pt), small open arrowhead — conveys "nothing extracted"
Card: rounded rectangle,
  Background: #FAFAFA, border: #E0E0E0 1px
  Content: just 2 tiny code lines in light gray (representing source-code-only input)
  Right-side accuracy badge: "75%" in 8pt, color #9E9E9E (gray, muted — not good)
  Visual density: very sparse, mostly white space inside the card

**Path 2 — exception_only (second from top) — THE STAR:**
Arrow: solid line, #2E7D32 (dark green), 1.5pt, filled arrowhead — conveys "targeted extraction"
Card: rounded rectangle with a subtle green left-border accent (4px, #43A047)
  Background: #F1F8E9, border: #A5D6A7 1px
  Content: 3 compact lines: "[ERROR] TypeError", "msg: unsupported operand", "stack: line 12"
  Text in 7pt monospace, #33691E
  Right-side accuracy badge: "99.8%" in 9pt BOLD, color #2E7D32, with a small star ★ icon
  Visual density: compact but focused — every line is meaningful
  **This card should visually "pop" — the green accent + star + bold accuracy clearly mark it as the winner**

**Path 3 — VOTA (third from top):**
Arrow: solid line, #1565C0 (dark blue), 1.2pt, filled arrowhead
Card: rounded rectangle with subtle blue left-border accent (3px, #42A5F5)
  Background: #E3F2FD, border: #90CAF9 1px
  Content: 4-5 lines including "[ERROR]...", "assert actual≠expected", "loop[×3]..."
  Text in 7pt monospace, #0D47A1
  Right-side accuracy badge: "98.5%" in 8pt, color #1565C0
  Visual density: moderate — more content than exception_only but still structured

**Path 4 — full_trace (bottom) — THE WARNING:**
Arrow: thick solid line, #E65100 (dark orange), 2pt, large filled arrowhead — conveys "everything dumped in"
Card: rounded rectangle with orange/red left-border accent (4px, #FF6D00)
  Background: #FFF3E0, border: #FFCC80 1px
  Content: 8+ tiny densely packed lines overflowing the card, some lines fade/clip at the right edge
  Lines should look like verbose trace output: "[Line 1] x = 5", "[Line 2] y = func(x)", etc.
  Text in 6pt monospace, #BF360C, packed tight
  Right-side accuracy badge: "81%" in 8pt, color #E65100, with a small down-arrow ↓ icon indicating degradation
  Visual density: OVERFLOWING — visually cramped and noisy, conveying information overload
  Optional: tiny "~2048 tokens" annotation below in 6pt gray

**Vertical bracket/brace** on the right side of all 4 cards, with label: "Information Density →" running vertically (bottom to top), indicating that density increases from no_trace to full_trace. Use a thin elegant brace in #78909C.

=== STAGE 4: MODEL + VERDICT (right, ~18% width) ===
All four paths converge (4 arrows merging) into a single box:
- "SFT Fine-tuning" label in 9pt serif bold
- Subtle neural network icon or a small LM icon (e.g., stacked layers)
- Background: #ECEFF1, border: #90A4AE, corner radius 10px

Then a final arrow → to a verdict output display:
- Two small icons: green checkmark ✓ "pass" and red cross ✗ "fail"
- Clean, minimal

=== CONNECTING ARROWS (global style) ===
All arrows: thin, elegant, tapered heads (not matplotlib's bulky default).
Arrow color: #90A4AE for neutral connections, colored for the 4 extraction paths.
Arrow heads: small triangular, filled, consistent size across all arrows.

=== OVERALL STYLE REQUIREMENTS ===
- 300 DPI, pure white (#FFFFFF) background
- Publication quality for a TOP venue (NeurIPS/ICML/EMNLP)
- Elegant, premium, sophisticated — NOT cheap or homework-like
- NOT a simple block diagram — this should have depth, nuance, visual storytelling
- Subtle drop shadows (2px, 6% opacity) on all major boxes
- Rounded corners (10px) on all rectangles
- Thin, elegant arrow heads — not bulky matplotlib defaults
- Serif font (Times New Roman) for labels and titles
- Monospace font (Courier) for code/trace content inside cards
- Sans-serif (Helvetica) for small annotations
- Muted, harmonious color palette — sage greens, steel blues, warm oranges — NO saturated neon colors
- Generous white space between elements — do not cram
- Consistent visual weight and baseline alignment across all 4 representation cards
- The 4 cards should be exactly the same width and height (uniform grid), only their CONTENT differs in density
- NO matplotlib default styling: NO gray figure background, NO thick gridlines, NO tab10 colors
- The figure should read clearly when scaled to single-column width (~3.3 inches) — all text ≥ 7pt at that scale
